official.deadline_note: Single PhD Track session for the 2026-2027 academic year ran 14 October 2025 - 20 January 2026 via the IP Paris online application platform. Master's applications via the IP Paris portal ran in three sessions ending 8 January 2026, 26 March 2026 and 28 May 2026 (the 3rd session is not open for every program). Registration (post-admission, not application) for 2026-2027 entrants opened 2 June 2026 and closed 31 July 2026. The official site states the dates for the next session will be announced on the website.
official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 cycle (most recent published); the PhD Track application period runs from October to January each year
official.status_note: The 2026-2027 PhD Track application session (14 October 2025 - 20 January 2026) has closed; the official page states the dates for the next session will be announced on the website. Admitted 2026-2027 students registered between 2 June and 31 July 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official wording: 'We also subsidize tuition fees for all PhD Track admitted students, whether they receive a scholarship or not: Years 1 and 2: fees reduced from approximately EUR 7,000 per year to EUR 243 per year. Years 3, 4, and 5: tuition fees set at EUR 380 per year.' The page notes these are the official tuition fees set by the Ministry of Higher Education and Research (MESR) for the 2023-2024 academic year and may change by decree; the FAQ adds 'All PhD Track students benefit from an attractive rate of 243 EUR.' The official 2026-2027 Master's Tuition Fees document lists the PhD Track rate at EUR 255 per year (EU/EEA and non-EU alike). Students receiving a Campus France scholarship do not pay tuition.
benefits: Master's excellence scholarship (EUR 10,000/year) for 2 years (or 1 year)

Full Package (FP): 5-year (or 4-year) funding, including a Master's excellence scholarship (EUR 10,000/year) for 2 years (or 1 year) and a doctoral funding commitment for 3 years - a total minimum gross funding of approximately EUR 82,800 over 3 years
Master's Scholarship (BM): 2-year (or 1-year) funding, including only a Master's excellence scholarship (EUR 10,000/year)
Doctoral Package (DP): 3-year doctoral funding commitment, covering only the doctoral studies - a total minimum gross funding of approximately EUR 82,800 over 3 years
Tuition fees subsidized for all admitted PhD Track students, whether they receive a scholarship or not: EUR 243 per year in years 1-2 and EUR 380 per year in years 3-5
Doctoral funding is paid as a monthly salary during the three doctoral years
eligibility: A Bachelor's degree (Bac+3 and 180 ECTS) or an international Bachelor's degree is required to apply for the PhD Track

Entry at M2 level requires an M1 certificate of completion (or equivalent - 180 ECTS + 60 ECTS completed); direct second-year entry may be offered to holders of a Master's degree or 60 ECTS in a Master's program
Applicants must be fluent in English, have an excellent academic background and wish to become researchers
Evidence of research potential is essential as the main goal of such a PhD program is to train first class researchers
General selection principles include enrollment at a highly ranked university, based on national rankings and/or the international QS rankings
requirements: Proof of English proficiency at B2 level (TOEIC, IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge ESOL), except for native speakers and students who have previously completed a program taught in English
Degrees and academic transcripts - all transcripts of records from the first university year onwards
Two academic references; the applicant must provide referee contact details and referees submit their recommendations online
Motivation letter / statement of purpose written specifically for each program applied to
A document certifying ECTS credits; for non-ECTS grading systems, an official document explaining the institution's grading system to establish an ECTS equivalence
documents: Degrees and academic transcripts (from the 1st year at university onwards)
Supporting statement / motivation letter written specifically for the program applied to (PDF)
Two letters of recommendation - contact information for two referents, who receive an automatic e-mail to complete an online recommendation form
English language proficiency certificate (minimum level B2) if not exempted as a native speaker or graduate of an English-taught program
Last diploma received, or a certificate of achievement if the diploma has not yet been awarded; an ID-size photograph (JPG/JPEG); official ECTS equivalence document where applicable
selection_criteria: The application is evaluated by an admissions jury, which decides admission to one or several programs
Admitted PhD Track files are automatically reviewed by a jury for the potential award of a PhD Track scholarship; non-selected candidates are placed on a funding waiting list
Excellent academic background and evidence of research potential ('to train first class researchers')
Enrollment at a highly ranked university, based on national rankings and/or the international QS rankings

For the doctoral phase, progression requires presenting the research project before the doctoral school jury and securing funding; Full Package and Doctoral Package holders who obtain an evaluation of at least A have their funding guaranteed
coverage: Master's excellence scholarship: EUR 10,000 per year for the Master's year(s)
Doctoral funding commitment: a total minimum gross funding of approximately EUR 82,800 over 3 years, paid as a monthly salary
Tuition fees: reduced from approximately EUR 7,000 per year to EUR 243 per year in years 1-2, and set at EUR 380 per year in years 3-5, for all admitted PhD Track students regardless of scholarship
application_method: Applications are submitted exclusively online and are file-based, via the IP Paris application portal (Master's IP PARIS & PhD Track IP PARIS)
No additional steps are required when applying to the PhD Track program - if admitted, the application is automatically reviewed by a jury for the potential award of a PhD Track scholarship
Candidates may apply to up to 5 programs, Master and/or PhD Track; each application is assessed independently and it is strictly forbidden to apply twice to the same program
For Physics tracks, the motivation letter must describe preferred fields of study and research, and candidates are encouraged to choose two preferred PhD Track subjects
official.application_route: Apply online through the IP Paris application portal during the October-January session; admitted PhD Track files are automatically reviewed by the scholarship jury - there is no separate scholarship application
official.international_eligibility: Yes - admission is open to candidates holding (or in the process of obtaining) a Bachelor's degree awarded by an institution equivalent to Institut Polytechnique de Paris, in France or abroad, and the PhD Track is taught in English
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to applicants to the 12 IP Paris PhD Track programs: Advanced Materials; Bioengineering and Quantitative Life Sciences; Chemistry and Interfaces; Computer Science; Data & Artificial Intelligence; Economics; Electrical Engineering; Energy for Climate; Mathematics; Mechanics; Physics; Quantum Science and Technologies (QUANTIX)
official.research_requirement: Evidence of research potential is essential ('the main goal of such a PhD program is to train first class researchers'); students must complete one research internship per year during the first two years, and progression to the doctoral phase requires presenting a research project before the doctoral school jury and finding a thesis supervisor
official.duration: 5 years (2-year Master's + 3-year PhD, 300 ECTS); a 4-year track is possible with direct entry into the second year
official.description: The Institut Polytechnique de Paris awards excellence scholarships each year to PhD Track students, covering their Master's years as well as doctoral funding commitments with a monthly salary. The five-year program offers training in top-level research to high-potential students aiming for an international career in leading academic institutions or companies.

applicant_utility.summary: IP Paris funds its 12 English-taught PhD Tracks through three packages: Master's-only (BM, EUR 10,000/year for one or two Master's years), doctoral-only (DP), or the Full Package (FP) that pairs the EUR 20,000 Master's stipend with a three-year doctoral funding commitment worth a minimum of roughly EUR 82,800 gross. Every admitted PhD Track student pays subsidized tuition regardless of whether they win funding, so the scholarship decision changes your stipend, not your fee status. The critical mechanic is that there is no separate scholarship form: your admission file is the funding application, and a jury screens admitted candidates automatically. October-January is the only application window, and campaign documents must be rebuilt for each of the up to five programs you can list.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent bachelor's graduates from highly ranked universities with top grades, real research experience (publications, internships, a strong referee who knows their lab work) and a committed plan to become a researcher in a STEM field
application_readiness_checklist: Write a fresh statement of purpose for each program - IP Paris assesses every application independently and warns that generic, recycled statements undermine files
Line up two academic referees in September: they must upload their recommendations themselves through the portal, and the applicant is responsible for chasing them before the January deadline
If your transcript is not ECTS-based, request an official grading-scale/equivalence document from your registrar early - it is a required upload, not an optional one
Convert your GPA to the French 20-point scale for the Academic Background section rather than leaving a raw foreign average for the jury to interpret
Book a B2 English test (TOEIC, IELTS, TOEFL or Cambridge ESOL) unless you are a native speaker or finished a degree taught in English, and keep the certificate PDF ready to upload
For Physics tracks, name two preferred PhD Track subjects and your research fields explicitly in the motivation letter
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete files: IP Paris warns that an incomplete application file may be automatically rejected - a missing ECTS document, missing diploma certificate or a referee who never submits kills the file before any jury sees it
Documents not in French or English without a sworn translation
Treating the scholarship as a separate application: candidates who assume a later funding call will come miss the fact that the jury review happens once, off the admission file

Weak research evidence: grades alone are not the target profile - the programme explicitly selects future researchers, and applicants with no internship, project or publication trail lose to peers who have one
Applying twice to the same program, which is strictly forbidden and detectable

Master's-only (BM) scholars who assume doctoral funding continues automatically: they must compete later in the doctoral school selection process, and only an evaluation of at least A guarantees the Full/Doctoral Package commitment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs: the IP Paris FAQ estimates a monthly budget of EUR 600-900 (about USD 730-1,100) to live in Paris. The Master's-phase EUR 10,000/year stipend must absorb most of this for BM holders, no travel or installation allowance is published, and PhD Track tuition (EUR 243-255 per year) is effectively negligible but not zero. Campus France scholarship holders pay no tuition, and a Financial Aid Commission and Tuition Fee Waiver Commission exist for students in serious financial difficulty
document_audit: Every document must be in French or English; anything else needs a sworn translation or it is incomplete
An ID-size photograph in JPG/JPEG is a separate upload that applicants routinely overlook
A certificate of achievement is acceptable if your final diploma has not been conferred yet, but the actual diploma/certificate must still be uploaded
Referees submit their own recommendations online - collecting PDF letters yourself does not satisfy the requirement
For the doctoral phase later, the file additionally needs the thesis project, M2 grades and a letter of support from the thesis supervisor, so keep an updated research record from year one
alerts: The window is short: the 2026-2027 PhD Track session ran only 14 October 2025 - 20 January 2026, and the next session's dates are simply 'to be announced' - monitor the official page from early October
Admission without funding is possible: unsuccessful scholarship candidates go on a funding waiting list rather than being rejected, so read your offer letter carefully for what it actually funds
The EUR 243/EUR 380 fee figures on the website are the MESR 2023-2024 rates and can change by decree; the official 2026-2027 fees document already lists PhD Track at EUR 255 per year

You can list up to five programs in one application, but applying twice to the same program is forbidden, and Master's-platform deadlines (three sessions ending 8 January, 26 March and 28 May) differ from the single PhD Track deadline
For Physics tracks you are encouraged to pick two preferred subjects in the motivation letter - leaving this blank wastes a selection signal
Registration after admission is a separate, hard deadline (31 July for 2026-2027 entrants) with a payment obligation and no refund on withdrawal
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account on the IP Paris application portal, complete the file and upload documents (referees receive an automatic link to submit online), submit before the session closes, then wait for the e-mail/candidate-space decision - issued within about two months of the session end, with the scholarship jury contacting successful candidates directly afterwards
